findings.title: `queued` default is evaluated once at import, so every instance gets the same timestamp
findings.body: `queued: datetime = timezone.now()` is a dataclass default, so `timezone.now()` runs once when the module is imported. Every AssignmentSource created in that process then carries the process-start time, not the time the assignment was queued. The value is serialized by `to_dict()` into the task payload. It should be `field(default_factory=timezone.now)`. The existing `test_to_dict` only asserts `queued is not None`, so it would not catch this.

findings.title: The actual inbound-webhook loop path and the deassign path are untested
findings.body: The new test calls `GroupAssignee.objects.assign` directly with a hand-built `AssignmentSource`. Nothing verifies that `sync_group_assignee_inbound` (the entry point used by the Jira webhook) passes `AssignmentSource.from_integration(integration)` through to `assign`/`deassign`. The `deassign` path with a matching source, which this PR also changes, has no test. The `assignment_source_dict` parsing in `sync_assignee_outbound` and the `should_sync` source-exclusion logic have no direct tests either. Without these, a regression that drops the source on the inbound path would reintroduce the loop with a green test suite.

findings.title: Loop check excludes the whole integration, not the originating external issue
findings.body: The check `sync_source.integration_id == self.org_integration.integration_id` suppresses outbound assignee sync to every external issue of that integration linked to the group. A group linked to two Jira issues on the same Jira site would no longer receive assignee updates to issue B when issue A's assignee is changed by an inbound webhook. The description only mentions preventing the echo back to the triggering issue. This suppression of legitimate updates to other linked issues is not mentioned or tested.

findings.title: New positional argument to `should_sync` and new kwarg to `sync_assignee_outbound` break existing overrides
findings.body: The task now calls `installation.should_sync("outbound_assignee", parsed_assignment_source)` and `installation.sync_assignee_outbound(..., assignment_source=...)` on every installation. Any installation subclass that still overrides `should_sync(self, attribute)` or a concrete `sync_assignee_outbound` without `**kwargs` will now raise TypeError, even when no assignment source is involved. The PR does not show a check that all overrides were updated.

findings.title: Unused `assignment_source` parameter added to the abstract `sync_status_outbound` contract
findings.body: The abstract `sync_status_outbound` signature gains an `assignment_source` parameter, but no caller in this PR passes it and no implementation is required to use it. The docstring still describes only the status propagation. This is a misleading contract change for implementers, unrelated to the assignee fix.

findings.title: `to_dict()` puts a raw datetime into a dict passed as a Celery task argument
findings.body: `asdict(self)` keeps `queued` as a `datetime`. This dict is passed as `assignment_source_dict` in `apply_async` kwargs (src/sentry/integrations/utils/sync.py, around line 141). A datetime is not JSON-native, so the type does not survive a JSON-serialized task round trip, and the consumer receives a string instead. Serializing `queued` to an ISO string, or excluding it, would make the payload type-stable.
